description: Disaster Behavioral Health Information Series is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by DHHS Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. In addition to their immediate physical effects, extreme weather events can also have substantial psychological consequences on people. For example, people may lose a loved one, lose their home, or be forced to relocate. To help people plan for disasters and cope with their aftermath, this webpage offers numerous resources on disaster-specific preparedness and response. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – General, High Winds, Wildfire. Assets: Cultural and Community Services, People. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
